item.title: ADAM BRICKER - Cinematographer
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 213 Adam Bricker - CinematographerIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with cinematographer Adam Bricker (HACKS, CHEF'S TABLE, AMERICAN VANDAL). After being hosted by Adam at several Q&A's around Los Angeles, we turn the tables on him, and we ask him about his own career, learning about his journey from Chicago to Los Angeles and the many hours he put in cold-calling filmmakers on Craigslist to pitch himself as a cinematographer. We also discuss the value of having an agent as a DP, and Adam reflects on the privilege of having been able to work in Los Angeles during an extended city-wide downturn in production shoot days. Adam was also the sole cinematographer across five seasons and nearly 50 episodes on HACKS, a comedy series on HBO MAX, and he reveals how he and the other filmmakers approached shooting the show, from location scouting and prepping to grabbing the footage on the day. Adam also reflects on nailing the final shot of the series, and he shares how he endeavored to imbue a single-camera sensibility into the multi-cam show. Plus, we discuss Adam's relationship with light meters.Recommended Viewing: HACKSThis episode is sponsored by BenQ & Aputure

item.title: Mike and Jay Talk About It Ends
item.author: RedLetterMedia
item.content:encoded: Mike and Jay both enjoyed a little film called "It Ends" and wanted to have a chat about it. Often cited as having a misleading ad campaign making the film look more like a horror movie about zombies trying to get you as you drive down a road in a car, the movie is more a laid back existential thriller about the most terrifying thing of all - having to be alive with your own nasty ass. Dealing with the shock that once you leave college and head out into the real world, that life is nothing but an endless series of holidays, routines, chores and then you die.

item.title: MOTHER MARY - with David Lowery
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 212 MOTHER MARY - with David LoweryIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, director David Lowery (Season 2, Episode 60) returns to discuss his latest film, MOTHER MARY, now available to stream at home. Throughout the episode, we discuss the making of the movie, and topics include: the origin of the two lead characters, shooting the dialogue-heavy script, the evolution of the concert footage, and filming the bulk of the movie in 2023 and the remainder in 2024. We learn how the "ghost" was visualized and captured practically, where the supernatural elements of the movie came from, how actress Anne Hathaway prepared for her character's elaborate dance choreography, and why the film was shot in Germany even though it's set in England. David also shares how the process of developing MOTHER MARY differed and mirrored the development of his other films. In addition to learning how David filmed the movie, we also discuss how much work was done in post, and David reveals the level of invisible VFX work in the final cut. Plus, David shares some information about his next project.Recommended Viewing: MOTHER MARYThis episode is sponsored by Aputure

item.title: Does RESIDENT EVIL equal WEAPONS? + JULIETTE BINOCHE
item.author: Kermode and Mayo's Take
item.content:encoded:
The Take is now on Patreon: www.patreon.com/kermodeandmayo Become a Vanguardista or an Ultra Vanguardista to get video episodes of Take Two every week, plus member-only chat rooms, polls and submissions to influence the show, behind-the-scenes photos and videos, the monthly Redactor’s Roundup newsletter, and access to a new fortnightly LIVE show - a raucous, unfiltered lunchtime special with the Good Doctors, new features, and live chat so you can heckle, vote, and have your questions read out in real time.
Legendary French actress Juliette Binoche is our special guest this week. She’ll be talking to Simon about her new film Queen at Sea, a hard-hitting drama examining the tensions and taboos of caring for a family member with Alzheimer’s. Plus we’ll hear a little about her dance documentary directorial debut In-I in Motion - which is also released in the UK this week. She even challenges Simon to get on the dancefloor…now that we would like to see…
Mark reviews Queen at Sea, as well as three more big screen releases - it is, as they say, a packed show. We’ll get his verdicts on Resident Evil - an adaptation of the hugely popular videogame from Weapons director Zach Cregger - as well as dark classroom satire Bad Apples, starring Saoirse Ronan, and the latest Aardman animated treat, Shaun The Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom.
Plus an uncharacteristically quite-funny Laughter Lift (which we really did need this week…), and all your excellent correspondence. Keep it coming please!
You can contact the show by emailing correspondence@kermodeandmayo.com or you can find us on social media, @KermodeandMayo.

item.title: EDDIE MARSAN - Actor
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 211 Eddie Marsan - ActorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with actor Eddie Marsan (NO ORDINARY HEIST, BACK TO BLACK, RAY DONOVAN). During our conversation, we discuss Eddie's youth in East London, being discovered by casting in a club at 18, his disciplined approach to his craft, working with a range of directors including Mike Leigh (Season 1, Episode 76), Edgar Wright (Season 2, Episode 169), and Steven Spielberg, playing a countless number of supporting roles, and the shortcomings of filmmakers who fail to give working and lower class characters volition, autonomy, and humanity. Eddie also reflects on acting as "evil" characters, and we discuss the qualities of several of them from throughout his career. Towards the end of the episode, we ask Eddie how younger generations of actors are different compared to the ones who came before, and he encourages young actors to not wait for the system to change and create space for the roles they want to play. Plus, Eddie reveals the type of character he'd love to play but has yet to.This episode is sponsored by Aputure

item.title: Vincent D’Onofrio’s Closet Picks
item.author: CRITERION
item.content:encoded:
Subscribe to Criterion: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCAP57cF-FSjJKzzXg7ntPlQ?sub_confirmation=1
The actor and director talks about the shock of seeing MAN BITES DOG for the first time, shares his admiration for Marcello Mastroianni’s subtly brilliant performances, and explains how his love for Liv Ullmann led him to the films of Ingmar Bergman.
Vincent’s Picks: THE RULING CLASS (Peter Medak, 1972)* MIDNIGHT COWBOY (John Schlesinger, 1969) MAN BITES DOG (Rémy Belvaux, André Bonzel, and Benoît Poelvoorde, 1992)* DIVORCE ITALIAN STYLE (Pietro Germi, 1961)* A WOMAN UNDER THE INFLUENCE (John Cassavetes, 1974)* DOWN BY LAW (Jim Jarmusch, 1986) INGMAR BERGMAN’S CINEMA*
Shop all the Picks from criterion.com: https://www.criterion.com/shop/collection/1005-vincent-d-onofrio-s-closet-picks
*Watch THE RULING CLASS, MAN BITES DOG, DIVORCE ITALIAN STYLE, A WOMAN UNDER THE INFLUENCE, and the films collected in INGMAR BERGMAN’S CINEMA (complete with the special features from the Criterion Collection disc releases) on our streaming service, the Criterion Channel: https://www.criterionchannel.com
During his visit to the Closet Vincent also shared his memories of working with Stanley Kubrick on FULL METAL JACKET. Watch that here, as part of our ongoing series leading up to the release of THE COMPLETE KUBRICK next month: https://youtu.be/QB3A7YbBrRo
